name: Serah
overview: Serah is a female member of the tribe of Asher, uniquely noted as the daughter of Asher. She is mentioned among the descendants of Israel who went down to Egypt, indicating her presence during this significant migration. Her identity is primarily grounded in her tribal affiliation and family lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Serah means 'one who explains, opens, extends; abundance.' This proper name, as recorded in Genesis 46:17, reflects themes of revelation and plenty, though it was not given by God directly.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Serah as the daughter of Asher, situating her within the family of one of Israel's sons. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Serah's mention as a daughter of Asher among those who journeyed to Egypt places her within the foundational narrative of Israel's descent into Egypt, a pivotal event in God's unfolding plan for His people. While her role is brief, her inclusion underscores the completeness of Israel's family during this period. Her presence connects the tribe of Asher to the larger story of God's providence in preserving His covenant people.
